This course, developed for FAA James Scholar students, explores the arts and culture in a major American City. The purpose is to examine, discuss and experience the American urban landscape from a cultural and historical perspective. The eight-week course culminates in a week-long visit to a major American city. During the visit, students will examine the city as a lived space, investigating its architecture, built environment, and public art along with experiencing live performances of dancers, musicians and actors. The course will expose FAA James Scholars to a wide range of visual, performance and environmental arts events in the city. James Scholar Field Trip $1500.00 Course Fee

For Sustainable Design majors only. Prior approval of internship is required; students are encouraged to inquire early whether an internship is eligible. Internships should be relevant to the field of Sustainable Design and may be paid or unpaid. Registration only with instructor permission (submit your internship job description and offer letter to sustaindesign@illinois.edu prior to the 1st day of class). Course is zero credit hours and graded as Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory. CPT that is tied to an elective course can no longer be approved.

To enroll in this course: You must have junior or senior standing and a 3.3 GPA minimum. Obtain consent of instructor and faculty administrator for Sustainable Design. A contract must be completed & approved. Email sustaindesign@illinois.edu to enroll.
